summary: No cookies and no trackers, so most privacy law stays quiet. The gaps were a missing privacy notice, an unlabelled AI-generated video, and one experience claim worded more broadly than the record behind it. All nine findings are now closed.

scope.why: Ontario business collecting personal information in commercial activity: emails to hello@, Cloudflare analytics.
Serves clients "across Canada"; confirm whether there are Quebec clients or visitors.
The site promotes services to people in Canada.
Photos, video, fonts and quoted recommendations are reproduced.
No newsletter or sign-up form on the site.
Website rule (WCAG 2.0 AA) starts at 50 employees in Ontario.
Markets services and shows testimonials to US clients.
Revenue far below USD 26.625M; nowhere near 100,000 California consumers.
No EU/UK targeting and no tracking. Ad pixels, Google Analytics or EU marketing would trigger it.
Nothing is stored on the visitor's device.
The AI-generated hero video is output used in the EU whenever an EU visitor views it (Art. 2(1)(c)).
No federal website rule for private businesses; litigation risk only.

first_visit.result: None, and none needed while nothing is stored on the device
Autoplay, muted, looping; no AI label, no pause control
Main site on HTTPS, but `http://` answered 200 without redirecting
robots.txt (allows all), llms.txt, sitemap.xml; no security.txt

findings.title: No privacy notice
findings.saw: No privacy, terms or cookie page linked anywhere. The site invites email to hello@aroojqureshi.com and loads Cloudflare Web Analytics.
findings.why: An Ontario business receiving prospects' emails and page-view data is collecting personal information in commercial activity.
findings.risk: A prospect asking "what do you do with my data?" finds nothing.
findings.fix: Publish /privacy, linked from the footer and contact section: who is accountable, what is collected, why, who processes it and where, retention, access and correction, how to complain (OPC; CAI for Quebec).
findings.fix_short: Publish a /privacy notice and link it from the footer and contact section.

findings.title: AI-generated hero video has no label
findings.saw: Realistic driver's-eye video (car, lake, bridge, city) made with Runway; no text says it is AI-generated.

clause.text: EU AI Act Art. 50(4), with Art. 3(60)

findings.why: The scene could pass as filmed footage; any EU visitor brings the output into the EU.
findings.risk: Low legal exposure, high credibility cost for an AI-governance adviser.
findings.fix: Label on the video ("AI-generated video") and an AI-use line in the footer. Keep the export's content credentials.
findings.fix_short: Add an "AI-generated video" label and a footer AI-use line.

findings.title: Experience claim overstates what is counted
findings.saw: "13+ years of production AI in regulated industries" on the homepage and in llms.txt; the years include education analytics and university research.

clause.text: Competition Act s. 74.01(1)(a); FTC Act s. 5

findings.why: Experience is the main reason a buyer picks an AI adviser, so the claim is material.
findings.risk: A buyer who counts the CV may doubt the rest of the page.
findings.fix: Reword to "13+ years in AI and data science, now in regulated industries (telecom and energy)"; update llms.txt and JSON-LD.
findings.fix_short: Reword to "13+ years in AI and data science, now in regulated industries".

findings.title: Plain HTTP served; no security headers
findings.saw: `http://aroojqureshi.com/` returned 200 with no redirect; none of five security headers sent.
findings.why: Visitors who type the address without https get an unprotected copy.
findings.risk: Low data exposure (no forms), but avoidable.
findings.fix: Redirect `http:` to `https:` (301) in the Worker; add HSTS, CSP, `nosniff`, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy to every response.

findings.title: Looping video: no pause control or text alternative
findings.saw: 11-second hero video autoplays and loops, hidden from screen readers, with no text equivalent.
findings.why: Best practice here (AODA threshold not met; ADA litigation risk in the US).
findings.risk: People who need motion to stop can't; screen-reader users miss the story.
findings.fix: Always-visible Pause/Play button; one visually hidden sentence describing the video.

findings.title: Link names don't match their visible text
findings.saw: axe `label-content-name-mismatch` on 4 elements: logo link and three "Read on LinkedIn" links.

clause.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.3 Label in Name (Level A)

findings.why: Voice-control users say what they see, and nothing happens.
findings.fix: Start each `aria-label` with the visible words, e.g. "Read on LinkedIn: From Data Silos to AI Silos".

findings.title: llms.txt behind the page
findings.saw: llms.txt missing the training offers added on 2026-11-17; repeated the claim in F3.

clause.text: Competition Act s. 74.01; FTC Act s. 5 (representations however delivered)

findings.why: AI assistants that read llms.txt describe an older business.
findings.fix: Regenerate llms.txt from the page content whenever the page changes.

findings.title: Testimonial permissions undocumented
findings.saw: Four quoted recommendations, relationships stated; one edited with "… [and]".
findings.why: The quotes promote services to Canadian and US buyers.
findings.fix: Keep each quote's source link and the person's OK on file.
findings.status_note: Owner confirmed: all are public LinkedIn recommendations.

findings.title: No security.txt
findings.why: Tells researchers how to report a problem.
findings.fix: Publish security.txt with a contact and an expiry date.

passes.item: Zero cookies and zero device storage before consent, so no banner is needed.
passes.clause: ePrivacy Art. 5(3); PECR reg. 6; Law 25 s. 8.1

passes.item: Fonts self-hosted with their licence files; visitors' IP addresses are not sent to Google Fonts.
Testimonials state the relationship ("former student", "former senior manager").
No prices and no performance percentages to substantiate.
FAQ structured data matches the visible FAQ.
passes.clause: Competition Act s. 74.01; FTC Act s. 5

passes.item: Page language set, image alt text present, www redirects to the main domain.

owner_to_confirm.question: Testimonial permissions (F8)
owner_to_confirm.answer: All four are public LinkedIn recommendations.

owner_to_confirm.question: Do you have Quebec clients or visitors? Decides whether Law 25 applies.
Which countries do visitors come from? EU or UK traffic raises the AI Act exposure.
Text contrast over the moving video: check by eye at the darkest and brightest frames.

coming_changes: **Canada, Bill C-36** (Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act), introduced 15 June 2026, would replace Part 1 of PIPEDA. Not law yet.
**Ontario AODA** is expected to move from WCAG 2.0 to WCAG 2.2.
**EU AI Act Art. 50(2)**: the AI tool provider's machine-readable marking duty applies to existing systems from 2 December 2026.
method: First-visit scan on 2026-11-17 from a GitHub-hosted runner, fresh Chromium profile identifying itself as website-governance-audit and obeying robots.txt; re-scanned after fixes the same day. The scan cannot see server-side logs, dashboard settings, emails sent or contracts with processors. Automated accessibility testing finds only part of the problems.
